blogs.title: When Behçet’s and Neuro-Behçet’s Debut Together: Diagnosing the MRI-Negative Presentation
blogs.description: Concurrent systemic BD and acute neuro-BD is rare and often MRI-negative early. This post walks through recognizing neuro-BD when mucocutaneous criteria accrue over days, interpreting CSF that suggests aseptic meningitis, applying the International Criteria (without over-relying on HLA-B51), and deciding when to repeat imaging or initiate treatment despite normal MRI.

blogs.title: Hyponatraemia Pointing to the Brain: SIADH as a Signpost in Acute Neuro-Behçet’s
blogs.description: Hyponatraemia with low serum osmolality, concentrated urine, and high urine sodium in a euvolaemic patient should raise SIADH—and in BD, it can be the earliest clue to CNS inflammation. We review the SIADH workup, the IL-6/neuroinflammation link, correcting sodium for hyperglycaemia, and how to exclude drug, pulmonary, and malignant causes in parallel.

blogs.title: The Hiccup, the CK, and the Fluid: Navigating SIADH’s Hidden Complications
blogs.description: Persistent hiccups and unexpected rhabdomyolysis can be underappreciated manifestations of profound hyponatraemia. This piece highlights checking CK in hyponatraemic neuroinflammation, and the bedside tension between fluid restriction for SIADH and volume needs for rhabdomyolysis, outlining pragmatic strategies to balance sodium correction safety with muscle protection.

blogs.title: Colchicine for Acute Neuro-Behçet’s: Outlier or Option?
blogs.description: Steroids remain first-line for acute neuro-BD, with immunosuppressants for refractory disease; colchicine is traditionally reserved for mucocutaneous BD. We examine this case of colchicine-responsive, MRI-negative neuro-BD, review mechanistic plausibility (neutrophil and cytokine modulation), the limits of existing evidence, and when a steroid-sparing trial might be reasonable in carefully selected, mild presentations.

blogs.title: Don’t Let the Labs Lead You: Smarter Testing in Suspected Neuro-Behçet’s
blogs.description: Broad panels (ACE, sIL-2R, autoantibodies) can distract when pretest probability is low. Using this case, we discuss a stepwise approach to CNS inflammation that prioritizes clinical features and time-course, interprets nonspecific markers cautiously, and embraces diagnostic re-calibration as new BD features (like genital ulcers) appear.

blogs.title: Empiric Now, De-escalate Fast: Antimicrobial Strategy in Aseptic Meningitis Mimics
blogs.description: Fever, headache, and hyponatraemia warranted early cefepime and acyclovir, but negative CSF studies supported timely de-escalation. This post reviews empiric coverage principles for suspected meningoencephalitis, pitfalls of early viral PCR timing, and safe off-ramps to avoid unnecessary antimicrobials once neuroinflammatory diagnoses like neuro-BD emerge.
